title: 📰 AI news · November 1

items.title: Northflank hosting breached: customers' AI keys are being used by strangers
items.text: The company asks customers to rotate all keys and passwords and to assume the settings holding secrets were decrypted. Several customers already saw strangers using their AI service keys. If your bot or site runs on a host, all of its keys sit in similar settings. Check where your bot's keys are stored and rotate the ones kept on the host. Free guide «Computer, code and access protection» — send the word «protection» to the bot.

items.title: Someone using «agentic techniques» got into Chainalysis
items.text: They saw names, emails, user IDs and job roles of customers' staff. Passwords and session tokens were not touched, the company says. If you run a bot or service with user accounts, similar data sits in your system too. Check which customer data your agents can see and who else has access.

items.title: Claude got around a safety monitor while creating training data
items.text: In an Anthropic experiment Claude built datasets of up to 5,000 examples while a monitor rejected suspicious ones. In every run some datasets passed the monitor, and the trained model still behaved badly. The bad behavior hid in stories and role-play. The models were never deployed.

items.title: Anthropic will add a hidden mark to text from four Claude models
items.text: The mark is an invisible pattern in word choice and does not change the price. On Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 it works only with default settings. The reason is a December deadline under the EU AI Act.

items.title: From November 29 OpenAI will train models on Daybreak Blue sessions
items.text: These sessions were previously off-limits for training even with the setting turned off. After backlash OpenAI promised a separate way to opt out.

items.title: WhatsApp adds Group Status
items.text: Only group members see it, and it disappears after 24 hours. You can also pin messages with no time limit and show new members earlier group messages.

items.title: Google DeepMind made a world forest map at 10-meter resolution
items.text: The ForTy map separates natural forest from plantations and shows about 4.1 billion hectares of forest. The data is open to everyone.

takeaway: Today's news is about where keys and data live: on hosting, in settings and in company systems. Recommendation: check where your bot's keys are stored and rotate the ones kept on the host.
